[[Image:Roughriders win3.jpg|thumb|The Roughriders celebrate their [[Grey Cup]] victory]]
The '''[[2007 CFL season|2007]] [[Saskatchewan Roughriders]]''' finished in second place in the West Division with a 12–6 record, which was their highest finish since 1988 when they also finished 2nd. The Roughriders won their third [[Grey Cup]] championship after playing the [[Winnipeg Blue Bombers]] for the title.

===Grey Cup===
{| class="wikitable"
! Team !! Q1 !! Q2 !! Q3 !! Q4 !! Total
|-style="background-color:#DDFFDD"
|[[Saskatchewan Roughriders]] || 0 || 10 || 6 || 7 || '''23'''
|-
|[[Winnipeg Blue Bombers]] || 3 || 4 || 7 || 5 || 19
|} <ref name="nationalpost.com">[https://nationalpost.com/sports/story.html?id=123061 Green glory: Riders win sloppy Grey Cup<!-- Bot generated title -->]{{dead link|date=October 2025|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref>

Saskatchewan ended the [[Canadian Football League]]'s longest championship drought with a 23–19 victory over the Winnipeg Blue Bombers in the [[95th Grey Cup]] at [[Rogers Centre]]. The Roughriders had not won a title since [[77th Grey Cup|1989]], and had lost in 13 of their 15 all-time appearances.<ref name="nationalpost.com"/>

An interception by defensive back [[James Johnson (Canadian football)|James Johnson]] with 54 seconds left in the fourth quarter sealed the victory. It also earned Johnson a place in CFL history – because he became the first player to intercept three passes in a Grey Cup game, and also because he was named the game's [[Grey Cup Most Valuable Player|MVP]].<ref name="nationalpost.com"/> Roughriders receiver Andy Fantuz was named the game's [[Dick Suderman Trophy|Most Outstanding Canadian]]. The 23-year-old caught four passes for 70 yards and a touchdown.<ref name="nationalpost.com"/>
